sanskrit: gurupradhāno dharmeṣu svayam arthānvavekṣitā dharmapradhāno lokeṣu suciraṃ mahad aśnute
english: He who holds his teacher foremost in matters of dharma, yet examines questions of profit for himself, and who keeps dharma foremost among the worlds — he long enjoys greatness.

sanskrit: vāmadeva uvāca yatrādharmaṃ praṇayate durbale balavattaraḥ tāṃ vṛttim upajīvanti ye bhavanti tadanvayāḥ
english: Vāmadeva said: Where the stronger man works injustice upon the weaker, those who follow in his train take up that same way of life and live by it.

sanskrit: rājānam anuvartante taṃ pāpābhipravartakam avinītamanuṣyaṃ tat kṣipraṃ rāṣṭraṃ vinaśyati
english: They follow that king who sets evil in motion, that ill-disciplined man — and swiftly does such a realm perish.

sanskrit: yad vṛttim upajīvanti prakṛtisthasya mānavāḥ tad eva viṣamasthasya svajano 'pi na mṛṣyate
english: The very conduct by which men live under a king who keeps his proper course, even his own kin will not endure in one who has gone astray.

sanskrit: sāhasaprakṛtir yatra kurute kiṃ cid ulbaṇam aśāstralakṣaṇo rājā kṣipram eva vinaśyati
english: Where a king of reckless temper does some monstrous deed, a king who bears not the mark of the scriptures swiftly comes to ruin.

sanskrit: yo 'tyantācaritāṃ vṛttiṃ kṣatriyo nānuvartate jitānām ajitānāṃ ca kṣatradharmād apaiti saḥ
english: The Kṣatriya who does not follow the conduct long established toward the conquered and the unconquered falls away from the dharma of warriors.

sanskrit: dviṣantaṃ kṛtakarmāṇaṃ gṛhītvā nṛpatī raṇe yo na mānayate dveṣāt kṣatradharmād apaiti saḥ
english: The king who, having captured in battle a hostile foe who has done his deeds well, fails out of malice to honor him, falls away from the dharma of warriors.

sanskrit: śaktaḥ syāt sumukho rājā kuryāt kāruṇyam āpadi priyo bhavati bhūtānāṃ na ca vibhraśyate śriyaḥ
english: Let the king, though powerful, be of gracious countenance, and show compassion in distress; thus he becomes dear to all beings and does not fall from his fortune.

sanskrit: apriyaṃ yasya kurvīta bhūyas tasya priyaṃ caret nacireṇa priyaḥ sa syād yo 'priyaḥ priyam ācaret
english: To one whom he has wronged, let him afterward do a greater kindness; for in a little while he becomes dear who, having displeased, then renders a pleasing deed.

sanskrit: mṛṣāvādaṃ pariharet kuryāt priyam ayācitaḥ na ca kāmān na saṃrambhān na dveṣād dharmam utsṛjet
english: Let him shun all false speech and do kindness unasked; neither from desire, nor from fury, nor from hatred let him cast off dharma.

sanskrit: nāpatrapeta praśneṣu nābhibhavyāṃ giraṃ sṛjet na tvareta na cāsūyet tathā saṃgṛhyate paraḥ
english: Let him not be shamed by questions, nor utter a word that can be assailed; let him not be hasty, nor envious — thus is another won over.

sanskrit: priye nātibhṛśaṃ hṛṣyed apriye na ca saṃjvaret na muhyed arthakṛcchreṣu prajāhitam anusmaran
english: In what is pleasant let him not rejoice overmuch, and in the unpleasant let him not be inflamed; let him not lose his bearings in straits of policy, ever mindful of the welfare of his people.

sanskrit: yaḥ priyaṃ kurute nityaṃ guṇato vasudhādhipaḥ tasya karmāṇi sidhyanti na ca saṃtyajyate śriyā
english: The lord of the earth who, by his virtues, ever does what is pleasing — his undertakings prosper, and fortune does not forsake him.

sanskrit: nivṛttaṃ pratikūlebhyo vartamānam anupriye bhaktaṃ bhajeta nṛpatis tad vai vṛttaṃ satām iha
english: Let the king favor the devoted man who has turned from hostile courses and walks in ways agreeable to him — for that, here, is the conduct of the good.

sanskrit: aprakīrṇendriyaṃ prājñam atyantānugataṃ śucim śaktaṃ caivānuraktaṃ ca yuñjyān mahati karmaṇi
english: The man of well-governed senses, wise, wholly loyal, pure, capable and devoted — him let the king employ in a great office.

sanskrit: evam eva guṇair yukto yo na rajyati bhūmipam bhartur artheṣv asūyantaṃ na taṃ yuñjīta karmaṇi
english: But even one so endowed with virtues, who feels no attachment to the king and who grudges his master's interests — such a man let him not employ in any office.

sanskrit: mūḍham aindriyakaṃ lubdham anāryacaritaṃ śaṭham anatītopadhaṃ hiṃsraṃ durbuddhim abahuśrutam
english: The dullard, the slave of his senses, the greedy, the ignoble in conduct, the deceitful, one who has not passed the tests of integrity, the cruel, the ill-minded, the unlearned —

sanskrit: tyaktopāttaṃ madyarataṃ dyūtastrīmṛgayāparam kārye mahati yo yuñjyād dhīyate sa nṛpaḥ śriyaḥ
english: the man who abandons what he has taken up, who is given to drink, addicted to dice, women, and the hunt — the king who employs such a one in a great task is cut off from his fortune.

sanskrit: rakṣitātmā tu yo rājā rakṣyān yaś cānurakṣati prajāś ca tasya vardhante dhruvaṃ ca mahad aśnute
english: But the king who guards himself and protects those who are to be protected — his subjects flourish, and he surely attains greatness.

sanskrit: ye ke cid bhūmipatayas tān sarvān anvavekṣayet suhṛdbhir anabhikhyātais tena rājā na riṣyate
english: Let him keep watch upon all the lords of the earth, whoever they may be, through trusted friends who go unrecognized; thus the king comes to no harm.

sanskrit: apakṛtya balasthasya dūrastho 'smīti nāśvaset śyenānucaritair hy ete nipatanti pramādyataḥ
english: Having injured one who is strong, let him not feel secure thinking, "I am far away"; for such men, ranging like hawks, swoop down upon him who grows heedless.

sanskrit: dṛḍhamūlas tv aduṣṭātmā viditvā balam ātmanaḥ abalān abhiyuñjīta na tu ye balavattarāḥ
english: Firmly rooted and of unblemished soul, having gauged his own strength, let him march against the weak — but not against those who are stronger than he.

sanskrit: vikrameṇa mahīṃ labdhvā prajā dharmeṇa pālayan āhave nidhanaṃ kuryād rājā dharmaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Having won the earth by valor and protecting his subjects by dharma, let the king, devoted to dharma, meet his end in battle.

sanskrit: maraṇāntam idaṃ sarvaṃ neha kiṃ cid anāmayam tasmād dharme sthito rājā prajā dharmeṇa pālayet
english: All this ends in death; nothing here is free from decay. Therefore let the king, established in dharma, protect his subjects by dharma.

sanskrit: rakṣādhikaraṇaṃ yuddhaṃ tathā dharmānuśāsanam mantracintyaṃ sukhaṃ kāle pañcabhir vardhate mahī
english: The office of protection, warfare, the administration of dharma, deliberation upon counsel, and timely ease — by these five the realm increases.

sanskrit: etāni yasya guptāni sa rājā rājasattama satataṃ vartamāno 'tra rājā bhuṅkte mahīm imām
english: He for whom these are kept secure — that king, O best of kings, ever abiding in them, enjoys this earth.

sanskrit: naitāny ekena śakyāni sātatyenānvavekṣitum eteṣv āptān pratiṣṭhāpya rājā bhuṅkte mahīṃ ciram
english: These cannot be watched over unremittingly by one man alone; setting trustworthy men over them, the king enjoys the earth for long.

sanskrit: dātāraṃ saṃvibhaktāraṃ mārdavopagataṃ śucim asaṃtyaktamanuṣyaṃ ca taṃ janāḥ kurvate priyam
english: The giver, the one who shares fairly, the man of gentle bearing, the pure, who does not abandon his people — him the people make their beloved.

sanskrit: yas tu niḥśreyasaṃ jñātvā jñānaṃ tat pratipadyate ātmano matam utsṛjya taṃ loko 'nuvidhīyate
english: But he who, recognizing the highest good, takes up that knowledge, casting aside his own opinion — him the world follows.

sanskrit: yo 'rthakāmasya vacanaṃ prātikūlyān na mṛṣyate śṛṇoti pratikūlāni vimanā nacirād iva
english: He who, out of contrariness, will not bear the word of one who seeks his good, shall before long, dejected, hear words contrary to his wishes.

sanskrit: agrāmyacaritāṃ buddhim atyantaṃ yo na budhyate jitānām ajitānāṃ ca kṣatradharmād apaiti saḥ
english: He who fails utterly to grasp the wisdom of a conduct above the common — toward the conquered and the unconquered alike — falls away from the dharma of warriors.

sanskrit: mukhyān amātyān yo hitvā nihīnān kurute priyān sa vai vyasanam āsādya gādham ārto na vindati
english: He who, forsaking his chief ministers, takes base men for his favorites, when calamity befalls him finds no firm ground in his deep distress.

sanskrit: yaḥ kalyāṇaguṇāñ jñātīn dveṣān naivābhimanyate adṛḍhātmā dṛḍhakrodho nāsyārtho ramate 'ntike
english: He who out of hatred holds in no esteem his kinsmen of excellent qualities — irresolute in soul, yet fixed in wrath — his fortune does not delight to dwell near him.

sanskrit: atha yo guṇasaṃpannān hṛdayasyāpriyān api priyeṇa kurute vaśyāṃś ciraṃ yaśasi tiṣṭhati
english: But he who, by kindness, makes obedient to him men endowed with virtues, even though they be unpleasing to his heart, abides long in renown.

sanskrit: nākāle praṇayed arthān nāpriye jātu saṃjvaret priye nātibhṛśaṃ hṛṣyed yujyetārogyakarmaṇi
english: Let him not press his interests out of season, nor ever be inflamed at what displeases him, nor rejoice overmuch at what pleases him; let him keep to wholesome action.

sanskrit: ke mānuraktā rājānaḥ ke bhayāt samupāśritāḥ madhyasthadoṣāḥ ke caiṣām iti nityaṃ vicintayet
english: Which kings are attached to me in love, which have taken refuge with me out of fear, and which among them are tainted by neutrality — this let him ever ponder.

sanskrit: na jātu balavān bhūtvā durbale viśvaset kva cit bhāruṇḍasadṛśā hy ete nipatanti pramādyataḥ
english: Having grown strong, let him never trust a weaker man in any matter; for these, like the bhāruṇḍa birds, swoop down upon him who grows heedless.

sanskrit: api sarvair guṇair yuktaṃ bhartāraṃ priyavādinam abhidruhyati pāpātmā tasmād dhi vibhiṣej janāt
english: Even a master endowed with all virtues and gentle of speech the evil-souled man will betray; therefore let him stand in wary dread of such people.

sanskrit: etāṃ rājopaniṣadaṃ yayātiḥ smāha nāhuṣaḥ manuṣyavijaye yukto hanti śatrūn anuttamān
english: This secret science of kings Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, proclaimed; intent upon the conquest of men, the king destroys even his most matchless foes.

sanskrit: vāmadeva uvāca ayuddhenaiva vijayaṃ vardhayed vasudhādhipaḥ jaghanyam āhur vijayaṃ yo yuddhena narādhipa
english: Vāmadeva said: Let the lord of the earth enlarge his victory without war; for the victory won through war, O ruler of men, they call the lowest kind.

sanskrit: na cāpy alabdhaṃ lipseta mūle nātidṛḍhe sati na hi durbalamūlasya rājño lābho vidhīyate
english: Nor let him seek to gain what he has not gained while his foundation is not yet firm; for to a king whose base is weak no gain is ordained.

sanskrit: yasya sphīto janapadaḥ saṃpannaḥ priyarājakaḥ saṃtuṣṭapuṣṭasacivo dṛḍhamūlaḥ sa pārthivaḥ
english: He whose realm is thriving and prosperous, whose people love their king, whose ministers are contented and well-nourished — that prince is firmly rooted.

sanskrit: yasya yodhāḥ susaṃtuṣṭāḥ sāntvitāḥ sūpadhāsthitāḥ alpenāpi sa daṇḍena mahīṃ jayati bhūmipaḥ
english: He whose warriors are well content, conciliated, and proven loyal under tests of integrity — that king conquers the earth with even a small army.

sanskrit: paurajānapadā yasya svanuraktāḥ supūjitāḥ sadhanā dhānyavantaś ca dṛḍhamūlaḥ sa pārthivaḥ
english: He whose townsfolk and countryfolk are well affected and well honored, rich in wealth and grain — that prince is firmly rooted.

sanskrit: prabhāvakālāv adhikau yadā manyeta cātmanaḥ tadā lipseta medhāvī parabhūmiṃ dhanāny uta
english: When the wise king judges both his power and the season to be in his favor, then let him seek to gain another's land and wealth.

sanskrit: bhogeṣv adayamānasya bhūteṣu ca dayāvataḥ vardhate tvaramāṇasya viṣayo rakṣitātmanaḥ
english: For him who spares not himself in indulgence yet is compassionate to all beings, who is diligent and self-controlled, the dominion grows.

sanskrit: takṣaty ātmānam evaiṣa vanaṃ paraśunā yathā yaḥ samyag vartamāneṣu sveṣu mithyā pravartate
english: He hews at his own self, as one hews a forest with an axe, who deals falsely with his own people when they conduct themselves rightly.

sanskrit: na vai dviṣantaḥ kṣīyante rājño nityam api ghnataḥ krodhaṃ niyantuṃ yo veda tasya dveṣṭā na vidyate
english: The enemies of a king who slays them perpetually are nonetheless never exhausted; but he who knows how to curb his wrath has no enemy at all.

sanskrit: yad āryajanavidviṣṭaṃ karma tan nācared budhaḥ yat kalyāṇam abhidhyāyet tatrātmānaṃ niyojayet
english: Let the wise man not do that deed which the noble hold in hatred; whatever is good, let him set his mind upon it and bend himself to it.

sanskrit: nainam anye 'vajānanti nātmanā paritapyate kṛtyaśeṣeṇa yo rājā sukhāny anububhūṣati
english: That king whom others do not despise, who is not consumed by self-reproach, and who seeks his pleasures only with what remains after duty is done —

sanskrit: idaṃvṛttaṃ manuṣyeṣu vartate yo mahīpatiḥ ubhau lokau vinirjitya vijaye saṃpratiṣṭhate
english: the lord of the earth who walks in such conduct among men, having conquered both worlds, is firmly established in victory.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity ukto vāmadevena sarvaṃ tat kṛtavān nṛpaḥ tathā kurvaṃs tvam apy etau lokau jetā na saṃśayaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus counseled by Vāmadeva, the king did all of it; and you too, by acting so, shall conquer both these worlds — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca atha yo vijigīṣeta kṣatriyaḥ kṣatriyaṃ yudhi kas tasya dharmyo vijaya etat pṛṣṭo bravīhi me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Now when one Kṣatriya seeks to conquer another in battle, what victory of his is righteous? Being asked this, tell it to me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sasahāyo 'sahāyo vā rāṣṭram āgamya bhūmipaḥ brūyād ahaṃ vo rājeti rakṣiṣyāmi ca vaḥ sadā
english: Bhīṣma said: With aid or without aid, a king, having entered a realm, should declare: "I am your king, and I shall ever protect you."

sanskrit: mama dharmyaṃ baliṃ datta kiṃ vā māṃ pratipatsyatha te cet tam āgataṃ tatra vṛṇuyuḥ kuśalaṃ bhavet
english: "Render unto me the tribute that is lawful — or how will you receive me?" If they then choose him who has come, it shall be well.

sanskrit: te ced akṣatriyāḥ santo virudhyeyuḥ kathaṃ cana sarvopāyair niyantavyā vikarmasthā narādhipa
english: But if those who are not Kṣatriyas should oppose him in any way, O ruler of men, they who stand in wrongful action must be restrained by every means.

sanskrit: aśaktaṃ kṣatriyaṃ matvā śastraṃ gṛhṇāty athāparaḥ trāṇāyāpy asamarthaṃ taṃ manyamānam atīva ca
english: Then another, deeming the Kṣatriya powerless, takes up arms, judging him utterly unable even to protect himself.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca atha yaḥ kṣatriyo rājā kṣatriyaṃ pratyupāvrajet kathaṃ sa pratiyoddhavyas tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Now when a Kṣatriya king marches against another Kṣatriya, how is he to be fought against? Tell me that, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nāsaṃnaddho nākavaco yoddhavyaḥ kṣatriyo raṇe eka ekena vācyaś ca visṛjasva kṣipāmi ca
english: Bhīṣma said: A Kṣatriya not arrayed for battle and without armor must not be fought in war; one is to be matched with one, and he should be told, "Loose your weapon, and I shall loose mine."

sanskrit: sa cet saṃnaddha āgacchet saṃnaddhavyaṃ tato bhavet sa cet sasainya āgacchet sasainyas tam athāhvayet
english: If he comes arrayed for battle, then one must array oneself; if he comes with an army, then with an army let one challenge him.

sanskrit: sa cen nikṛtyā yudhyeta nikṛtyā taṃ prayodhayet atha ced dharmato yudhyed dharmeṇaiva nivārayet
english: If he fights with treachery, with counter-stratagem let one fight him; but if he fights by dharma, then by dharma alone let one ward him off.

sanskrit: nāśvena rathinaṃ yāyād udiyād rathinaṃ rathī vyasane na prahartavyaṃ na bhītāya jitāya ca
english: Let him not assail a chariot-warrior with cavalry; a chariot-warrior should advance against a chariot-warrior. One must not strike at a man in distress, nor at one who is afraid, nor at one already vanquished.

sanskrit: neṣur lipto na karṇī syād asatām etad āyudham jayārtham eva yoddhavyaṃ na krudhyed ajighāṃsataḥ
english: Let no arrow be smeared with poison, nor be barbed — such is the weapon of the wicked. One must fight only for victory; let him not rage against one who seeks not to slay.

sanskrit: sādhūnāṃ tu mithobhedāt sādhuś ced vyasanī bhavet savraṇo nābhihantavyo nānapatyaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: But if, through a falling-out among the good, a good man should come to grief, he must not be struck if he is wounded, nor in any case if he is without offspring.

sanskrit: bhagnaśastro vipannāśvaś chinnajyo hatavāhanaḥ cikitsyaḥ syāt svaviṣaye prāpyo vā svagṛhān bhavet nirvraṇo 'pi ca moktavya eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: The man whose weapon is broken, whose horse is fallen, whose bowstring is cut, whose mount is slain — he should be tended in one's own domain, or be enabled to reach his own home; and even if unwounded he must be set free. This is the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: tasmād dharmeṇa yoddhavyaṃ manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo 'bravīt satsu nityaṃ satāṃ dharmas tam āsthāya na nāśayet
english: Therefore one must fight by dharma, so Manu the self-born declared; the dharma of the good is ever upheld among the good — abiding in it, let him not bring it to ruin.

sanskrit: yo vai jayaty adharmeṇa kṣatriyo vardhamānakaḥ ātmānam ātmanā hanti pāpo nikṛtijīvanaḥ
english: The Kṣatriya, waxing in power, who conquers by unrighteousness, slays himself by himself — a wicked man, living by treachery.

sanskrit: karma caitad asādhūnām asādhuṃ sādhunā jayet dharmeṇa nidhanaṃ śreyo na jayaḥ pāpakarmaṇā
english: This is the way of the wicked; let one conquer the wicked by good means. Better is death in righteousness than victory by an evil deed.

sanskrit: nādharmaś carito rājan sadyaḥ phalati gaur iva mūlāny asya praśākhāś ca dahan samanugacchati
english: Unrighteousness, once done, O king, does not bear fruit at once, like the earth; but, burning, it comes after its doer's roots and branches alike.

sanskrit: pāpena karmaṇā vittaṃ labdhvā pāpaḥ prahṛṣyati sa vardhamānaḥ steyena pāpaḥ pāpe prasajjati
english: Having gained wealth by an evil deed, the wicked man rejoices; and that wicked man, waxing by theft, clings ever more to evil.

sanskrit: na dharmo 'stīti manvānaḥ śucīn avahasann iva aśraddadhānabhāvāc ca vināśam upagacchati
english: Thinking, "There is no such thing as dharma," mocking, as it were, the pure-hearted, through his unbelieving disposition he comes to destruction.

sanskrit: sa baddho vāruṇaiḥ pāśair amartya iva manyate mahādṛtir ivādhmātaḥ svakṛtena vivardhate
english: Bound by the nooses of Varuṇa, he yet fancies himself immortal; swollen like a great leather bag, he keeps puffing himself up by his own doing.

sanskrit: tataḥ samūlo hriyate nadīkūlād iva drumaḥ athainam abhinindanti bhinnaṃ kumbham ivāśmani tasmād dharmeṇa vijayaṃ kāmaṃ lipseta bhūmipaḥ
english: Then he is swept away root and all, like a tree from a river's bank; and men revile him, like a pot shattered upon a stone. Therefore let the king, if he would, seek his victory by dharma.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nādharmeṇa mahīṃ jetuṃ lipseta jagatīpatiḥ adharmavijayaṃ labdhvā ko 'numanyeta bhūmipaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Let not the lord of the world seek to conquer the earth by unrighteousness; what king, having won a victory by unrighteousness, would approve of it?

sanskrit: adharmayukto vijayo hy adhruvo 'svargya eva ca sādayaty eṣa rājānaṃ mahīṃ ca bharatarṣabha
english: A victory bound up with unrighteousness is fleeting and bars the way to heaven; it brings down both the king and his realm, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: viśīrṇakavacaṃ caiva tavāsmīti ca vādinam kṛtāñjaliṃ nyastaśastraṃ gṛhītvā na vihiṃsayet
english: The man whose armor is shattered, who says, "I am yours," who folds his hands in supplication and has laid down his weapon — having captured him, one must not do him harm.

sanskrit: balenāvajito yaś ca na taṃ yudhyeta bhūmipaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ vipraṇayet tasmāj jātaḥ punar bhavet
english: He who has been overcome by force — the king must not fight him further; let him keep him in custody for a year, and thereafter he becomes as one reborn.

sanskrit: nārvāk saṃvatsarāt kanyā spraṣṭavyā vikramāhṛtā evam eva dhanaṃ sarvaṃ yac cānyat sahasāhṛtam
english: A maiden carried off by force must not be touched before a year is out; and even so all wealth and whatever else has been seized by violence.

sanskrit: na tu vandhyaṃ dhanaṃ tiṣṭhet pibeyur brāhmaṇāḥ payaḥ yuñjīran vāpy anaḍuhaḥ kṣantavyaṃ vā tadā bhavet
english: Yet the wealth should not stand idle and barren; let the Brāhmaṇas drink the milk, or let the oxen be yoked to labor — or else forbearance may then be shown.

sanskrit: rājñā rājaiva yoddhavyas tathā dharmo vidhīyate nānyo rājānam abhyased arājanyaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: By a king a king alone is to be fought — thus is the dharma ordained; no other, who is not of royal blood, should in any way assail a king.
